name: The lake shore sands

function.note: The beach along the North Side (Sheahan and Upton, pp. 113-114).

built.note: Natural shore; the year only opens the record.

research_note: THE LAKE SHORE SANDS by the old City Cemetery and Lincoln Park, built by T-3689 for the 1871 scene: the open shore where the people of the North Side fled from the fire on Monday 9 October 1871. Refugees were 'at Lincoln Park and the old cemetery to the south of it, and along the Lake-shore Drive' (Colbert and Chamberlin, p. 265); 'along the beach were judges, merchants, doctors, workingmen, women and children' (Sheahan and Upton, pp. 113-114). The strip follows the 1871 plan's shore line (Mitchell's 1870 map) along the cemetery; how wide the sand ran is reconstructed.

documented_range.note: The shore of Mitchell's 1870 map; the scene's phase begins in 1860.

position.symbolic_location: The lake shore along the old City Cemetery, north of North Avenue.
position.note: Along the 1871 plan's shore line from (845.06, 2703.29) to (638.19, 3392.44) (data/context/1871/plan.json, from Mitchell's 1870 map), on the level ground 16 to 40 m inland of the plan's line, above the bank. The footprint's origin is local E 818.24 N 2695.24.

derivation.reason: Laid along the plan's traced shore line; the 1871 beach's width was not surveyed.
